The hash covers cfg['payload'] AND NOTHING ELSE; every sibling key of 'payload' (schema_version, status, hash_algorithm, payload_sha256, and any key beginning with '_') is outside the hashed object by construction, so this file can carry its own digest. Verified at run start; mismatch => HALT_CONFIG_HASH_MISMATCH. features.visual_readout: CLIPVisionModel.pooler_output, per frame, mean-pooled within window
features.segment_cache_schema: {video_ids: [V] str (FLAT), subclip_img_feats: [V*K, Dv] float32, subclip_parent: [V*K] long, labels: [V*K] long, num_subclips: K, num_frames: M}
features.wholevideo_cache_schema: {ids: [[V] str] (NESTED - one sublist), img_feats: [V, Dv] float32, text_feats: [V, Dt] float32, labels: [V] long}
features.wholevideo_ids_contract_source: src/utils/generate_VideoCLIP_embedding_HF.py:14-15,395-397 ('# CONTRACT: ids is a list containing ONE sublist of all string ids.')
disclosures: the text half is constant across k, so all within-video discrimination comes from the visual half; this is not a temporal-text capability
A0 and A1 do not share a frame budget: A0's whole-video cache was built at num_frames=8, A1-A4's segment cache at M=120; max(A0,A1) absorbs it in criteria 1-3

hatemm_train_wholevideo.num_frames_note: the whole-video cache stores no num_frames key; 8 is the extractor default and is asserted against the extraction command line, never against the artifact

extraction_commands.recorded_in: feature_manifest.json (command line, git commit, HF_HUB_OFFLINE, encoder id, output sha256)
extraction_commands.failure_rule: if extraction fails or its asset-audit assertions fail, the affected confirmation stops with HALT_MISSING_ASSET; never a substituted endpoint, never a performance negative

temporal_grid.second_positive_rule: second t positive iff (t + 0.5) lies in a gold span
temporal_grid.frame_time_convention: endpoint-index: sampled frame j of M sits at normalized time j/(M-1), matching _sample_frame_indices = round(linspace(0, N-1, M)) (generate_subclip_embedding_HF.py:135-147). NOT the frame-midpoint convention (m+0.5)/N.
temporal_grid.sampling_alignment_proof: M=120, _window_bounds(120,30) gives base=4 rem=0 (generate_subclip_embedding_HF.py:236-259), so window k receives sampled frames 4k..4k+3 at normalized times [4k/119,(4k+3)/119]; 4k/119 >= k/30 for all k>=0 and (4k+3)/119 <= (k+1)/30 for all k<=29, so every sampled frame of window k lies strictly inside nominal window k; the k=29 right edge is exact (119/119=1.0) and the last window is closed at D
temporal_grid.applies_to_hateclipseg: yes - scripts/slurm/hateclipseg_subclip.sbatch runs the same K=30 / M=120 configuration

data.mhc_role: not a Gate-0 development dataset (prereg sec 0)

hatemm.val_use: one-time confirmation after all choices are frozen (see confirmation_protocol)
hatemm.test_use: SEALED - never opened by any code path
split_source_resolution_order: 1. data/gt/HateMM/train.jsonl exists (LIVE BRANCH): assert set(jsonl_ids) == set(cache['ids'][0]) and per-id label equality -> split_source='gt_jsonl'
2. else feature-cache embedded ids/labels from cache['ids'][0] and cache['labels'] -> split_source='feature_cache_embedded'
3. any mismatch in step 1 -> HALT_SPLIT_MISMATCH (never silently prefer one source)
hatemm.gold_spans_observed_schema: {video_id: {duration: float|null, spans: [[start_s,end_s]], label: 0|1, clipped?: bool, anomaly?: [str]}}
hatemm.gold_spans_schema_note: 'parse_error' is emitted by hatemm_spans.py only on a hard parse failure and does NOT occur in the current file; it is not asserted. The observed field set is recorded at asset audit.
hatemm.id_label_match_assertion: PASSED at asset audit 2026-08-07 for BOTH partitions: set(jsonl_ids) == set(cache['ids'][0]) and per-id label equality; HALT_SPLIT_MISMATCH did not fire

hateclipseg.binding_endpoint: has at least one segment labelled hateful vs none
hateclipseg.endpoint_supervision_status: consumed ONLY as a video-level binary label (training target, selection target, evaluation target). No per-segment gold label, no gold segment boundary, and no gold-derived segment mask/weight/pooling set ever enters any deployable path. The endpoint derivation returns a single int per video and discards the segment list before returning. No HateClipSeg temporal metric is computed in Gate-0.
hateclipseg.underpower_rule: if either class has < 10 videos in the P11 validation split, report the confirmation as underpowered and do not use it to satisfy any criterion
hateclipseg.any_toxic_endpoint: descriptive only; cannot replace a failed binding confirmation

binding_endpoint_counts_observed.underpower_check: both classes >= 10 in the P11 validation split; rule not triggered

failure_accounting.zero_vector_videos_definition: UNION across both caches: all 30 segment vectors exactly zero OR the whole-video img_feats row exactly zero
failure_accounting.zero_vector_retention_rationale: keeps the evaluated video set bit-identical across arms, as prereg sec 5.1 matching requires
failure_accounting.missing_duration_definition: duration null or <= 0 in the gold duration source
failure_accounting.halt_rule: |zero_vector_videos union missing_duration_videos| / V > 0.01 on HateMM-train => HALT

zero_vector_videos.hateclipseg_corpus_provenance_note: the extractor reported exactly 1 zero-vector video (yt_NzvfkIYS5Yg) over the full 395-video corpus; it is a p11_split['test'] id and is discarded by the sealed-id restriction, so every restricted count is 0. Recorded from the extraction log, not from a restricted read.

sealed_id_restriction.rationale: hate_spans.json spans the FULL HateMM corpus (1083 records incl. the sealed test set, each with a label); HateClipSeg gold/duration/split files and the whitelisted caches span all 395 videos incl. the 119 p11_split['test'] ids. Prereg sec 2.3 forbids LOADING official test labels/spans/per-example artifacts, which a path guard alone cannot prevent.
sealed_id_restriction.reader: load_corpus_spanning(path) - the ONLY admissible way to open these artifacts; it restricts the returned object to the currently authorized id set and DISCARDS every other entry BEFORE returning
sealed_id_restriction.phase_switch: unlock_confirmation() - callable AT MOST ONCE in the whole run; writes confirmation_unlock_utc to manifest.json; a second call is a HALT
assertions: ONLY AUTHORIZED IDS SURVIVE: set(restricted_ids) subset of authorized_ids. This is WHITELIST semantics - the reader keeps authorized_ids intersect file_ids and drops everything else - so no sealed id can survive BY CONSTRUCTION, whatever the sealed splits contain
sealed_ids_dropped = len(file_ids) - len(restricted) > 0 for every corpus-spanning file (a zero drop count means the restriction did not run)
no p11_split['test'] id survives the restriction (free - p11_split.json is already read to build the HateClipSeg authorized set and contains ids only)
sealed_id_restriction.hatemm_test_jsonl_check: the review's additional 'no HateMM test.jsonl id survives' assertion is REDUNDANT under whitelist semantics and is deliberately NOT implemented: assertion 1 is strictly stronger (it excludes every unauthorized id, not just the test ones), and the weaker check would require opening a sealed per-example artifact for no additional guarantee. Prereg sec 2.3 is satisfied with ZERO contact: test_contact_count stays 0 and opened_test_paths stays [] with no exception carve-out.

protocol.fold_implementation: sklearn.model_selection.StratifiedKFold(n_splits, shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the SORTED video-id list, stratified by the video-level binary label
protocol.primary_metric_aggregation: concatenate all outer-query predictions and compute once; never average fold metrics
protocol.infeasible_fold_rule: if either class has fewer members than the fold count => HALT_FOLD_INFEASIBLE
selection_loop: for each outer fold f and each registered config cfg: initialize 4 inner models (seeded per inner fold); advance ALL FOUR IN LOCKSTEP one epoch at a time
after each epoch: pool the 4 inner-held-out score sets FOR THAT EPOCH, derive theta by the threshold rule, compute pooled inner-OOF macro-F1
track best-so-far with min_delta=1e-4 and patience=40; break the epoch loop on stall; candidate[cfg] = (best, best_epoch, best_theta)
(cfg*, epoch*, theta*) = argmax over candidate[.] of best; ties -> smaller epoch, then smaller cfg index
refit ONCE on the full outer-train with cfg*, exactly epoch* epochs, inner=-1 seed
score outer-query(f) ONCE and apply theta*
assert one-query-fold-per-video, zero train/query overlap at video/segment/derived-id level, inner nested in outer-train
protocol.epoch_selection_rule: SINGLE rule: the patience-truncated best-so-far epoch per config, then argmax across configs with the global tie rule. The truncation IS part of the registered rule and is applied identically to every arm, config and fold. (v1's contradictory 'argmax over all epochs' and the false claim that early stopping cannot change the selection are both removed.)

optimization.lr_grid_note: 1e-2 added post-review (OP-6 free recommendation, accepted): costs a few CPU-minutes and removes the 'you under-fit A3' objection from any future NO-GO-A-SELECTOR writeup
optimization.l2_regularization_mechanism: AdamW weight_decay only, applied to all parameters including biases; no separate explicit L2 term
optimization.tie_break_rule: smaller epoch; then smaller index in the registered config list
tie_break_consequences: lr ties favour the larger lr
optimization.budget_alignment: identical optimizer, grid, epoch cap, patience, min_delta, batch size, loss, dtype, device and loop structure for every arm; arm-local grids (k for A2, tau for A4) are registered by the prereg and are additional; realized run counts and wall-clock are reported per arm in metrics.json.budget_report
optimization.recorded_limitation: batch_size=64 with drop_last=false means the outer refit takes more gradient steps at epoch* than an inner fit did (outer-train is ~33% larger); standard nested practice, compliant with prereg sec 7 step 3, applied identically to every arm

thresholding.candidate_set: midpoints of consecutive unique pooled inner-OOF scores, plus (min - 1e-6) and (max + 1e-6)

seeds.temporal_bootstrap_note: a SEPARATE draw over the sorted eligible video list, not a filtering of the master indices
seeds.generator_separation: rng4 (B4) and rng5 (B5) are SEPARATE numpy.random.default_rng instances so B5's draw cannot be perturbed by B4's consumption; both are consumed in ascending sorted video-id order

A1.pooling: mean over k of s[v,k], then head
A1.head: nn.Linear(d, 1) (separate instance from A0, refit)
A1.identity_note: head is affine so head(mean_k s) == mean_k head(s) exactly

A2.operand_consistency: identical definition in training and evaluation
A2.formula: z[v,k] = w.s[v,k] + b ; T = indices of k largest z (ties -> smaller window index) ; logit_v = mean_{j in T} z[v,j]
A2.soft_relaxation: none (hard top-k; gradient flows only through selected segments)
A2.head: nn.Linear(d, 1)
A2.arm_local_selection: pooled inner-OOF macro-F1; ties resolve to smaller config index, hence smaller k
A2.singleton_implementation_note: the per-segment score reduction must be implemented in closed form (z[v,k]); calling torch.topk(z,k=2) on a one-element tensor raises

A3.architecture: h_k = tanh(W s[v,k] + c) ; a_k = u.h_k ; alpha = softmax(a) ; p_v = sum_k alpha_k s[v,k] ; logit_v = w.p_v + b
A3.gated_rationale: the gated ABMIL variant is a different architecture; exactly one instantiation is registered; non-gated chosen for lower parameter count and simpler fixture-verifiable behaviour
A3.supervision: video-level BCE only; no entropy/sparsity/auxiliary loss; no segment target
A3.alpha_diagnostic: the within-video second-level AUROC computed from the attention weights alpha_k is recorded as a PRE-REGISTERED DIAGNOSTIC; it may never rescue a failed criterion 5 and never enters any decision

capacity_limitation.statement: A3 has ~231k parameters vs ~1.8k for A0/A1/A2/A4; the prereg installs a capacity control only in Gate-B (B3). Adding one to Gate-A would be a new arm, forbidden by prereg sec 11.1.
capacity_limitation.bound_1: prereg criterion 5 is itself the capacity/selection discriminator: a pure capacity effect raises video-level macro-F1 without localizing, and Gate-A requires ALL SIX criteria
capacity_limitation.bound_2: D is chosen among A2/A3/A4 and A2/A4 are ~1.8k-parameter arms; if D is A2 or A4 the confound is moot for the promoted arm
capacity_limitation.required_record: any Gate-A pass with D = A3 must carry the sentence 'the A3 advantage over A0/A1 is not capacity-controlled at Gate-A' in verdict.json

A4.operand: SCALAR SEGMENT LOGITS (same definition as A2)
A4.formula_rationale: the -log K term makes the operator interpolate mean (tau -> inf) and max (tau -> 0+) on the same scale as the logits
A4.head: nn.Linear(d, 1)
A4.arm_local_selection: pooled inner-OOF macro-F1; ties resolve to smaller config index, hence smaller tau

O1.segment_scorer: the A1 fold-trained linear head (no new parameters)
O1.rule: pool z over windows having POSITIVE-duration overlap with an annotated hate span; if that set is empty, fall back to registered A1 mean pooling over all K windows
O1.label_branching: forbidden - the routine may inspect span presence only
O1.threshold: own threshold from pooled inner-OOF O1 scores under the registered threshold rule
O1.threshold_reading_ratified_by_review: prereg sec 3's 'must not affect thresholds' governs DEPLOYABLE arms; gold spans may be read by the named non-deployable oracle/evaluation routines. A gold-blind threshold would make the oracle bound meaningless since O1's scores live on a different scale.

O2.segment_scorer: the A1 fold-trained linear head (no new parameters)
O2.rule: argmax_k z if gold label == 1 else argmin_k z; ties -> smaller k
O2.justification: the label-aware optimum of mean_{k in S} z over non-empty subsets S is attained at a singleton
O2.guaranteed_inequality: per video, O2_logit >= O1_logit when y=1 and <= when y=0 (asserted at run time)
O2.threshold: own threshold from pooled inner-OOF O2 scores under the registered threshold rule

segment_score_definition.rule: seg_score_arm(v,k) = sigmoid( f_arm({ s[v,k] }) ) - the arm's own scoring function on the singleton bag containing only that segment

consequences.A3: head(s[v,k]) because a singleton bag gives alpha = 1; and since p_v = sum_k alpha_k s[v,k] with an affine head, logit_v = sum_k alpha_k * head(s[v,k]) exactly, so head(s[v,k]) IS segment k's own contribution to A3's video logit
consequences.A0: video score broadcast to every second; within-video AUROC is exactly 0.5 by construction

segment_score_definition.a3_attention_weights: recorded additionally as a PRE-REGISTERED DIAGNOSTIC; NOT the registered score; may never rescue a failed criterion
segment_score_definition.implementation_note: implement the closed-form reduction per arm; do not route a singleton bag through the generic pooling function

arm_D.definition: argmax over {A2, A3, A4} of POOLED-INNER-OOF-MACRO-F1
arm_D.pooled_inner_oof_macro_f1_definition: concatenate the inner-held-out predictions of ALL 5 OUTER FOLDS, each fold contributing its own selected (cfg*, epoch*) at its own theta*, and compute ONE macro-F1 on that single concatenation; never a mean of per-fold macro-F1 values (same convention as prereg sec 7's primary metric)
arm_D.tie_break: arm id order A2 < A3 < A4
arm_D.selection_source: inner-OOF only; no outer-query prediction, no val, no test, no oracle
arm_D.recorded_property: the quantity is selection-optimistic (each fold's cfg*/epoch*/theta* were chosen to maximize that fold's own inner-OOF macro-F1) but is computed identically for A2/A3/A4, is used only to RANK them, and is never reported as a performance number
arm_D.written_to: metrics.json (identity, per-fold cfg*/epoch*/theta*, and the three aggregated numbers) before any Gate-B computation

d_score_source.outer_query_videos: D's outer-fold model at that fold's cfg* and epoch*
d_score_source.outer_train_videos: D's INNER-OOF predictions within the outer-train partition, produced by D's inner-fold models AT THAT OUTER FOLD'S SELECTED cfg* AND epoch* (never in-sample)

pair_selection.i1: argmax over k of D's registered per-segment score; ties -> smaller k
pair_selection.i2: argmax over {k : |k - i1| >= 2}; ties -> smaller k
pair_selection.slot_order: temporal (a = min(i1,i2) first, b = max(i1,i2) second)
pair_selection.supervision: video labels only (D never saw a span or segment label)

shared_trunk.projection: P = nn.Linear(d, r), r = 128, default init, one instance per arm

relative_time_encoding.positions: tA = iA/(K-1), tB = iB/(K-1) computed from the PRESENTED slots

B1.note: P linear so this equals P of the mean of the top-two segment representations; no interaction term, no phi

B2.interaction_term: elementwise product p*q in the projected space
B2.bilinear_rejected: a full bilinear form is d^2 parameters and is not registered

B3.hidden_rule: H3 = argmin over positive integers of |params(B3) - params(B2)|; ties -> smaller H3
B3.head_capacity_check: B2's 390->64->1 is 25024 parameters vs B3's 128->193->1 at 25090 (0.26% apart), so the match is NOT an artefact of the shared projection

B4.rule: independent per-video Bernoulli(0.5) swap of the presented slots, drawn once with numpy.random.default_rng(20260807) over the SORTED video-id list; the same draw is used in training and evaluation
assertions: realized swap fraction in [0.40, 0.60] else HALT
for every swapped video sign(delta_B4) = -sign(delta_B2) and iA > iB and in_B4 != in_B2
no downstream code re-sorts slots by time
unswapped videos have in_B4 bitwise equal to in_B2
the realized swap set is IDENTICAL between the training pass and the evaluation pass
B4.swap_fraction_bound_rationale: widened from [0.45,0.55] post-review: at V~744 the fraction has SE~0.018 so [0.45,0.55] is +-2.7 sigma and would trip ~0.7% of the time with NO legal recovery (the seed is prereg-pinned); [0.40,0.60] is +-5.5 sigma and still catches a broken or degenerate draw. The exact realized fraction is recorded in metrics.json regardless.
B4.always_swap_rejected: an unconditional swap is an invertible relabelling: phi_B4 = [t_b, t_a, -delta, |delta|, -sin(pi delta), cos(pi delta)] carries the same information as phi_B2, so a B4-trained model relearns the reversed convention, B2 - B4 ~ 0 by construction, and Gate-B would return a near-certain FALSE NO-GO-B regardless of whether temporal order matters

B5.legal_support_partition: outer_train(f) minus the query itself, for BOTH training rows and held-out query rows; never crosses an outer fold; a query video never donates to another query video
B5.matching_key: Dpred - D's frozen binary prediction at D's frozen inner-OOF threshold (inner-OOF for outer-train videos, outer-fold model for query videos)
B5.donor_contribution: the donor's own e_second under D's top-two selection
B5.replaced: content of the second slot only
B5.retained: the query's own phi (its true positions and offset)
B5.rationale: isolates identity of the second evidence unit from the temporal relation, which is B4's job; without this split the two lesions would be confounded and the two +0.015 criteria would not be testing different things
B5.rng: numpy.random.default_rng(20260807), a separate generator instance from B4's, consumed in ascending sorted video-id order
B5.fallback: if the Dpred-matched stratum is empty, draw uniformly from the full legal pool and set b5_fallback=true

msc_subset.membership: the set of AUDITED VIDEOS OF ANY CATEGORY (audited false negatives AND the 30 TP + 30 FP controls) carrying multi_segment_complementary as PRIMARY OR SECONDARY cause, per prereg sec 4.3's presence rule

rescue.formula: |{v in msc, label=1 : B0 predicts 0 and B2 predicts 1}| / |{v in msc, label=1 : B0 predicts 0}|
rescue.reporting: exact numerator/denominator and a Wilson 95% interval
rescue.zero_denominator: record 'not_evaluable' and treat the criterion as NOT SATISFIED (a rescue criterion with nothing to rescue cannot license a pass)

false_positive_side_condition.formula_in_counts: FP_arm = |{v in msc, label=0 : arm predicts 1}| ; criterion: FP_B2 <= FP_B0 + max(1, ceil(0.10 * FP_B0))
false_positive_side_condition.counts_not_ratio_rationale: expressed in counts so the 0/0 case cannot arise as a ratio (a nan compares False under every comparison, giving an accidental auto-pass or crash)
false_positive_side_condition.no_label_0_member: record 'not_evaluable' and treat the side condition as SATISFIED (it is a do-no-harm guard, not a positive requirement)

msc_subset.asymmetry_is_deliberate: the rescue rate is a positive requirement (unmet => fail); the FP condition is a do-no-harm guard (vacuous => pass)
msc_subset.recorded_note: with <=120 audited FNs and prereg sec 4.3's msc >= 15% floor the label-1 subset could be ~18 videos; the prereg sets no minimum; exact counts plus a Wilson interval are the registered treatment and the writeup must not over-read the rate

decision_inputs.primary: B2 - max(B0,B1,B3) >= +0.020 with paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero

confirmation_protocol.binding: prereg sec 5.2 item 6 and sec 6 bullet 4 are BINDING pass conditions, so the procedure is registered in full
confirmation_protocol.timing: runs ONCE, after every outer-OOF number is computed and every choice is frozen, immediately after the single unlock_confirmation() call
confirmation_protocol.prohibition: a confirmation set may not select an arm, threshold, epoch, granularity, config or decision rule (prereg sec 2.1, sec 8.1); no quantity below is derived on val

hatemm_val.scoring_model: ONE refit on the ENTIRE HateMM-train partition per arm
hatemm_val.cfg_val: the modal cfg* across the 5 outer folds; ties -> smaller registered config index
hatemm_val.epoch_val: median of the 5 outer folds' epoch* (odd count -> exact median)
hatemm_val.theta_val: median of the 5 outer folds' theta* (odd count -> exact median)
hatemm_val.seed: derive_seed({stage, arm, dataset:'HateMM', outer:-1, inner:-1, config:cfg_val})
hatemm_val.scoring: score HateMM-val ONCE with that single model and apply theta_val unchanged; the threshold is never re-derived, re-optimized or tie-broken on val
hatemm_val.segment_scores_on_val: D's per-segment scores come from D's val-refit model under the singleton rule; Gate-B pair selection on val uses those scores through the unchanged selection procedure
hatemm_val.b4_b5_on_val: not needed - prereg sec 6's val condition is on the B2 delta only

hateclipseg_val.selection: 4 inner video-stratified folds on HateClipSeg-train, seed 20260808, the SAME selection loop, the SAME config list and tie rule, the SAME threshold rule -> (cfg*, epoch*, theta*) from pooled inner-OOF only
hateclipseg_val.no_outer_loop: HateClipSeg-val is the evaluation set, not an OOF construction
hateclipseg_val.refit: ONCE on all of HateClipSeg-train, cfg*, exactly epoch* epochs, seed = derive_seed({stage, arm, dataset:'HateClipSeg', outer:-1, inner:-1, config:cfg*})
hateclipseg_val.scoring: score HateClipSeg-val ONCE and apply theta* unchanged
hateclipseg_val.what_transfers: ONLY D's arm identity (A2, A3 or A4)
hateclipseg_val.what_is_reselected: D's arm-local value (k or tau), lr, weight_decay, epoch and theta are re-selected on HateClipSeg-train inner-OOF under the identical registered grid
hateclipseg_val.transfer_rationale: prereg sec 2.2 admits only matched method comparisons on the identical surviving IDs; fitting every arm identically on HateClipSeg-train satisfies that, whereas transferring a HateMM-fitted head would be a domain-transfer experiment that is not the registered comparison. Feature family and dimensions are identical across datasets, so architectures transfer unchanged.
hateclipseg_val.weak_supervision_statement: the binding endpoint (has >= 1 segment labelled hateful) is DERIVED from gold segment labels but is consumed ONLY as a video-level binary label - training target, selection target, evaluation target - exactly as prereg sec 3 permits. No per-segment gold label, no gold segment boundary, and no gold-derived segment mask/weight/pooling set enters any deployable path. No HateClipSeg temporal metric is computed in Gate-0, so gold segment boundaries are never read beyond the endpoint derivation, which returns a single int per video and discards the segment list before returning.
hateclipseg_val.underpower_rule: report the binding-endpoint class counts in the P11 validation split; if either class has < 10 videos the confirmation is underpowered and cannot satisfy any criterion

confirmation_protocol.single_pass_discipline: manifest.confirmation_passes{hatemm_val, hateclipseg_val} must each be 1; a second pass is a HALT

temporal.eligible_video_rule: label == 1 AND >= 1 parsed gold span AND duration valid AND the video contains at least one positive and at least one negative evaluated second
temporal.primary_temporal_metric: mean over eligible videos of within-video second-level AUROC using the registered per-segment score
temporal.temporal_bootstrap: a SEPARATE draw from numpy.random.default_rng(20260809) over the sorted eligible video list, 10000 resamples, saved as bootstrap_indices.npz:temporal; not a filtering of the master indices; criterion 5 is a point-estimate threshold and the CI is reported, not binding
temporal.a0_comparator: video-score broadcast, which is exactly AUROC 0.5 per eligible video
temporal.a3_alpha_diagnostic: within-video second-level AUROC computed from alpha_k; non-binding
temporal.gold_span_recall_definition: fraction of eligible videos for which at least one of the n highest-scoring windows has positive-duration overlap with a gold span
separation_metrics: mean(gold-overlapping window scores) - mean(other window scores), averaged over eligible videos

bootstrap.scheme: within each label stratum draw n_label indices with replacement over the SORTED outer-OOF video-id list
bootstrap.multiple_testing_adjustment: none (one ordered decision path, one promoted arm)

gate_c.prediction_source: A0 whole-video baseline, HateMM-train only, the same 5 outer folds and the same inner-OOF threshold rule

sampling.tercile_basis: OOF positive-class score WITHIN the FN population
sampling.tercile_cut: numpy.quantile(scores_FN, [1/3, 2/3], method='linear'); tercile(v) = 0 if s < q33 else (1 if s < q67 else 2)
sampling.deficit_redistribution: if a tercile has fewer than its target, cap it at its size and reassign the deficit to the other terciles in ascending tercile index order, respecting their capacity

weights.formula: w[v] = N_{tercile(v)} / n_{tercile(v)} (full-population count over sampled count)
weights.coverage_formula: coverage(M) = sum_{v in audit_FN with mech(v) intersect M nonempty} w[v] / sum_{v in audit_FN} w[v]
weights.mechanism_presence: primary cause OR recorded secondary cause
weights.bootstrap: 10000 resamples, seed 20260809, resample n_t audited items with replacement within each tercile and reapply the FROZEN weights; percentile 95% CI

field_constraints.secondary_causes: zero or more taxonomy values, must not contain primary_cause
field_constraints.required_modalities: at least one of visual, speech, on_screen_text, audio_nonspeech, transcript
field_constraints.span_video_duration_ratio: computed as union(minimal_sufficient_intervals)/D_v, not typed by the annotator
field_constraints.notes: free text, used by no criterion

battery.name: span-localized signal

battery.name: global signal only
battery.construction: positives get +0.20*e1 on EVERY window; no localization

battery.name: oracle ordering
battery.construction: F1 plus sign-flipped noise spikes on a random 20% of windows
assertions: per-video O2_logit >= O1_logit when y=1 and <= when y=0 for 100% of videos

battery.name: ordered pair interaction
battery.construction: patterns pA=+1.5*e1 and pB=+1.5*e2; label 1 iff pA at window i and pB at window j with j-i >= 2; label 0 videos have j < i or only one pattern

battery.name: single segment sufficient
battery.construction: label 1 iff pA occurs anywhere; no pair structure

battery.name: B5 fallback
battery.construction: force Dpred constant 1 for all but 2 outer-train videos in one fold so the Dpred==0 stratum is empty for some queries

battery.name: degenerate assets
battery.construction: 3% all-zero segment videos, 2 videos zero only in the whole-video cache, 2 videos with duration=null, 5 positives with an empty span list
assertions: zero_vector_videos equals the UNION count across both caches
o1_fallback count equals the span-less video count
missing-duration videos excluded from eligible_videos but still receive video predictions
zero videos retained in every arm

battery.name: threshold rule

assertions: (b) the one closer to 0.5 is selected

battery.name: fold and leakage integrity

outer_train intersect outer_query empty at video, segment and derived-id level

items.text: fixture script path: appendix/payload wrote scripts/analysis/tera_gate0_fixtures.py, the actual file is scripts/tera_gate0/fixtures.py -- the payload field is updated
the fixture spike amplitude is defined relative to the L2-normalized window vector's scale (read literally as raw N(0,1), F1 could never pass)
F1's text half is a fixed vector shared by all videos (per-video noise would drown A1's visual block)
F2 is constructed as within-video same-window signal with amp 0.35 (at the registered 0.20 with independent windows, F2's own A1 >= A0 - 0.02 is unreachable; the O1 == A1 property is unchanged)

F4's negative-class mixture (20% inverted / 80% single-pattern) was unspecified in the appendix; the D segment scores used for pair selection are injected through a fixture-only hook (d_segment_scores_file, refused outside --fixture-mode, recorded in metrics.json)
F6's empty-stratum construction: inside the fold, force Dpred = 1 for everything except the 2 designated query videos, which are forced to 0
F7 keeps the registered categories and counts but uses V = 800 so the union is 0.875% <= 1% (the original 3% contradicted F7b's >1% HALT test)
F11's (150,130,120) tercile split is unreachable under sec 11.3's quantile rule; the assertion is split into three sub-assertions
F5 needs --fixture-mode's forced_stage_b to reach NO-GO-B
O1/O2 scores are taken as sigmoid(pooled logit) so they sit on the [0,1] scale the shared threshold rule expects
B5's rng5 is re-instantiated per outer fold and consumed in ascending video-id order; the Gate-B train-side pair construction uses D's outer-OOF segment scores
